sections.skill: Describe an agent's goal, tools, plan, feedback and stopping condition

questions.prompt: "Find three venues under 500 dollars for 40 people" is which part?

choices.text: Tool, because finding venues is something that a search tool does for the agent

questions.intro: An agent can be described with five parts. GOAL: what it is trying to achieve ("find three venues under 500 dollars for 40 people"). TOOLS: what it can use (search, calendar, email). PLAN: the steps it chooses (search, compare, list). FEEDBACK: the results it checks to decide what next (a venue is full, so look again). STOPPING CONDITION: when it must stop (three venues found, 20 searches done, or a question it cannot answer). A vague goal or missing stopping condition can make an agent wander, repeat steps, or take actions nobody intended.

sections.skill: Compare an agent's parts with sending someone grocery shopping

questions.prompt: "Ingredients for tacos for 6" is which part?
questions.intro: Sending a friend shopping has the same parts. GOAL: "ingredients for tacos for 6." TOOLS: your list, money and a car. PLAN: which stores and aisles. FEEDBACK: "they are out of tortillas, so try the bakery." STOPPING CONDITION: "come back once you have everything or after spending 40 dollars." Without that last part, your friend might drive to five stores looking for one item.

sections.title: Apply it

sections.skill: Prevent misread goals and runaway loops

questions.prompt: An agent told "get the most sign-ups" sends ten emails to each person. What went wrong?
questions.intro: Goals can be misread. "Get the most sign-ups" might lead an agent to send far too many emails, because nothing said not to. Good goals include LIMITS ("no more than one email per person") and say what to do when uncertain ("ask me before contacting anyone new"). A stopping condition should include a budget of time, steps or money, so a confused agent stops instead of looping. Ask the agent to report its plan before acting when the stakes are high.

questions.prompt: Which goal includes a useful limit?

choices.text: "Invite as many people as you possibly can, using any method you think will work."
"Invite club members, no more than one email each."
